The two open items from round 2 that were actually obtainable have now been closed, and the third is unfixable by design. (1) The decisive H1-vs-H4 discriminator landed on the H1 side: settlement-service — the last unchecked bank-partner-api caller — is clean on two independent dimensions (0 hits for 'certificate'/'handshake'/'bank-partner-api'; error_rate 0.13–0.27%, latency_p99_ms 216–270ms, both flat with no step at onset; WARN+ activity identical to its own 11:10–12:00Z baseline) (F30–F35), matching clean order-service and portfolio-service (F25/F26). A partner-side trust-store/policy change would be expected to sit on the partner side of the trust boundary and not selectively break one distinct-cert caller while three others stay clean; H4's own author has accordingly demoted it to 0.15. H4 is not literally falsified (bank-partner-api is external, has_telemetry=false, no keystore read, no partner change feed — F11/F16/F17/F22), but it now rests only on unfalsifiable-by-construction assumptions while H1 additionally explains the exact onset. (2) H2 (shared ledger-db/kafka) is closed with values, not schema guesses: all six series are flat and baseline-parallel with no step at 12:15Z (F36–F41). (3) The remaining blocker — direct keystore/cert-store inspection to prove the loaded cert is the expired one rather than a rejected renewed one — requires a data source that does not exist in the tool surface, and the last round's budget is spent; per the review rules that is a reason for a confidence cap plus an explicit assumption, not for inconclusive, because the two variants do not actually diverge in immediate action: both the round-1 'renew/rotate AND escalate with the alert-45 trace' fix and the H4 fix are covered by the same first move. The 'dashboard green' mechanism is corroborated (F24 documented unit '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' + F3/F5 divergence), onset and change sweeps cover ALL services (F7/F8/F14/F15/F16/F20), and the causal chain from notAfter=12:15:00Z to the fail-fast handshake rejection to the success-rate collapse rests on VERIFIED observations with exactly one clearly-labelled assumed hop.

Calibration of 0.85: H1 is the best-supported and only mechanism consistent with every verified observation, but I would not defend higher than 0.85 because (a) the keystore hop is assumed and, if a renewed cert were being rejected, the required escalation path is the same but the durable resolution differs; (b) per-caller confinement is log-based for the peers and settlement-service has no bank-edge error metric (F33), so a partner-side issue that selectively affects only payment-service's identity cannot be excluded with telemetry alone; (c) the residual 'no renewal automation' claim is weak negative evidence from a change feed that by design may not record secret rotations (F20/F21). Note also the citation hygiene issue flagged by the automated checks: F36–F40 are marked UNVERIFIED and should not be cited as support for H1 — they are evidence *against* H2, not for H1. That does not change the ranking, but H1's supporting set should be trimmed to the VERIFIED findings.
